model: Specialty insurer free cash flow to equity capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; after-tax underwriting plus investment earnings after interest, less capital retained to support premium growth, net debt zero)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-0.2%) diverges >30% from revenue (6.0%) and EPS (19.4%): Assurant distributes ~78% of earnings, and AOCI swung -$150M -> -$986M -> -$544M on bond marks, so book value is not a growth signal. EPS 3yr CAGR (49.7%) runs off a catastrophe- and investment-loss-depressed FY2022 base ($5.05). Owner-FCF CAGRs (65.9% 3yr, 5.2% 5yr) track float growth, not owner cash; the SBC-adjusted 3yr CAGR matches reported, i.e. SBC is not outgrowing cash flow. Revenue 3yr CAGR (7.9%) is the anchor, corroborated by H1-2026 revenue +10.3% YoY and the FY2026 Global Lifestyle low-double-digit guide.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2024-25 mobile carrier and OEM wins keep scaling: revenue +9% in FY2026 fading to 3%, and underlying pretax margin at a cat-normalised 9.9% rising to 10.3%. 30% of each revenue dollar added is retained as capital, and the rest is paid out through buybacks and dividends.
scenario_narratives.bull: Trade-in, upgrade and bundle programmes keep winning partners, and automation lifts margins. Revenue grows at a high-single to low-double-digit rate for three years, and the underlying pretax margin reaches 11.5%. Fee-heavy growth needs less capital.
scenario_narratives.bear: A major partner is lost at renewal, which stalls and then shrinks revenue. Cat losses and reinsurance costs run high while falling rates cut investment income, taking the underlying pretax margin to 8.3%, and capital retention rises.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Assurant is valued as a specialty insurer that pays out its earnings. The flow is after-tax underlying earnings, after interest, normal catastrophes and reserve development, less the capital regulators and rating agencies require to support premium growth, discounted at a 9% cost of equity with no net debt. Reported OCF minus capex is not used because it includes float growth. Book-value compounding is not used because book does not compound at a ~78% payout.
key_risks_to_valuation: Partner concentration in Connected Living: losing one large carrier or OEM contract is the bear case
Catastrophe severity and reinsurance pricing in Global Housing; the FY2026 base assumes a normal H2
Net investment income is ~45% of pretax income; lower yields compress the margin
Capital retention per dollar of growth (30% base) is inferred from tangible equity/revenue, not a disclosed requirement; actual FY2023-25 retention ran higher (~45%) while the ratio rebuilt
Excess holding-company liquidity is not credited (small upside)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 206.03-303.94
data_sources.financials: research/AIZ/Reports/AIZ_Metrics.csv; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1267238) for pretax income, investment gains/losses, net investment income, D&A, withholding taxes, unsecured debt, goodwill, AOCI, diluted shares through the Q2-2026 10-Q
data_sources.qualitative: research/AIZ/Reports/AIZ_Analysis.json (Q2-2026 results and raised FY2026 outlook)

bridge.item: Anchor refresh (price, shares, balance-sheet date unchanged -- same day)
Methodology change: OCF-based owner FCF at 8.5% WACC less holdco net debt -> insurer FCFE after growth-capital retention at 9% cost of equity, net debt zero
bridge.note: Opposing effects inside one method switch. Lowering the flow from reported OCF, which includes float growth (FY2025 owner FCF $1,499M), to FCFE after growth-capital retention (~$649M FY2025 proxy) cuts value. The prior build re-anchored its base to a mid-cycled $1,193M and ramped the EBITDA margin; this build instead drops the ~$509M holdco net-debt deduction (interest is already in the flows), which adds value, and moves the discount rate from 8.5% to 9.0%, which cuts it. Per-scenario: bear 159.05 -> 210.10, base 365.68 -> 334.61, bull 562.48 -> 433.95. The distribution narrows because the bear no longer runs on OCF swings and the bull no longer capitalises float growth.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 49.38m basic shares at 2026-06-30 (10-Q CommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~0.45m dilutive awards; Q2-2026 weighted diluted count 49.8m. Held FLAT: SBC and award withholding taxes are expensed in the flows, and buybacks are simply how the FCFE is distributed -- shrinking the count as well would double-count the same cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement ShareBasedCompensation $85.7M + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $13.8M (SEC XBRL companyfacts); no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the two are summed. Withholding spiked to $32.2M in H1-2026, hence 0.80% of revenue in year 1.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the flow is post-interest FCFE. USD build: ~4.2% 10-year UST + beta ~0.85 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.5%, plus 0.5pp for partner concentration and catastrophe tail that the three scenarios only partly span -> 9.0%, the same rate used for IAG.AX, the folder's other general-insurer FCFE build. Single rate across scenarios; downside is carried in the bear flows, not a higher rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases immaterial for an insurer of this size; lease cost sits inside GAAP pretax income, which is the flow anchor. No lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.holdco_debt_memo: Senior unsecured notes $2,208.1M at 2026-06-30 (us-gaap:UnsecuredDebt); consolidated cash $1,698.7M, almost all of it inside regulated subsidiaries backing policyholder liabilities. Neither is in the bridge: interest expense (~$110M/yr) is already deducted in the pretax margin, and subsidiary cash is float, not distributable. Holding-company excess liquidity above the ~$225M buffer is NOT credited -- a small conservatism.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2025 FCFE proxy, not reported-FCF minus SBC: GAAP net income $872.7M + after-tax investment losses ($71.8M x 0.79 = $56.7M) = $929.4M underlying; - award withholding $13.8M; + D&A $250.0M - capex $235.5M; - capital retained for growth (30% x $936.8M revenue increase = $281.0M) = ~$649M (5.1% of revenue). Reported FCF $1,598.4M (OCF - capex) is 1.8x net income because it includes growth in unearned premium and claims reserves -- float that must stay invested behind policyholder liabilities, not owner cash. That is why the owner-FCF route is wrong for this ticker.
inputs.notes: MODEL: insurer FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the same family as IAG.AX / GMG.AX / CHC.AX. Routing: SKILL.md sends insurers to BVPS compounding x exit P/B; that is overridden because Assurant does not compound book -- it pays out most of its earnings (FY2022-25 dividends $627M + buybacks $1,377M = 78% of cumulative net income $2,552M), so equity went $5.94bn FY2020 -> $5.87bn FY2025, and an exit P/B would just restate the answer as an assumed multiple. The prior 2026-09-25 Sonnet build used an owner-FCF DCF on OCF minus capex at an 8.5% WACC minus holdco net debt. That is rejected here: an insurer's OCF includes float growth (UPR $20.9bn, investments $10.5bn rising ~$0.9bn/yr), which is not distributable. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = GAAP total revenue (net earned premium $10.48bn + fees + net investment income $527M; the investment income is operating for an insurer because the portfolio backs policyholder liabilities). 'ebitda_margin' = pretax margin excluding investment gains/losses + SBC % (0.67) + D&A % (1.85), so the engine's EBIT equals underlying pretax income after interest expense, amortisation of intangibles and normal catastrophes, less the extra cash cost of award withholding. da_pct is set equal to capex_pct (1.85%) so acquired-intangible amortisation ($109M) is treated as a recurring cost of maintaining the partner book. cash_tax_rate 21% (FY2026 ETR guide 19-21%; FY2023-25 cash tax average 20.6% of pretax). wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE: statutory and rating-agency capital retained per dollar of revenue growth. Tangible equity ex-AOCI (equity - goodwill + AOCI deficit) has run at 25.6-29.9% of revenue (FY2022 25.6%, FY2025 29.4%), and actual incremental retention FY2023-25 was ~45% of the revenue increase while the ratio rebuilt. Base 30% holds the ratio at today's level; bull 25% (fee-heavy Lifestyle growth needs less statutory capital); bear 35% (rating-agency and cat-driven capital build). Retention above the steady-state ratio is treated as excess capital that is not valued unless it is distributed. ANCHORS: underlying pretax margin (ex investment gains/losses) FY2023 7.9%, FY2024 8.4%, FY2025 9.0%, H1-2026 10.8%, TTM 10.3%. The TTM is flattered by a light catastrophe run: the 2025 Atlantic season had no US hurricane landfall and the Q1-2025 LA wildfires have dropped out. FY2026E base = H1 actual $743.9M + H2 at a cat-normalised ~9.0% on ~$7.1bn revenue = ~9.9% of ~$13.96bn; the $71M adverse prior-year reserve development guided for FY2026 ($42M already booked in H1) is inside this. Recurring investment losses (~$70M/yr pretax FY2022-25, mostly portfolio repositioning that lifts NII) are excluded from the margin anchor; the bear margin path absorbs a reversal of the NII tailwind (100bp on a ~$9bn fixed-income book = ~0.7pp of margin). BUYBACKS: a funded repurchaser -- $303.7M FY2025, $201.8M H1-2026, guided to the top of $300-350M for FY2026 -- which is the distribution of the FCFE modelled here. Historical growth anchor is revenue, not equity (see historical_growth).
inputs.historical_owner_fcf_memo: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - withholding) FY2022 $328.5M, FY2023 $856.3M, FY2024 $1,015.1M, FY2025 $1,498.9M: shown for audit only; it tracks float growth, not distributable cash.

bear.margin_note: Underlying pretax 9.3% (H1 locked in, heavy H2 hurricane season) falling to 8.3% as a partner is lost, reinsurance costs rise and a lower-rate environment cuts NII ~0.7pp.
bear.narrative: A major US carrier or OEM moves device protection in-house or to Asurion at renewal. Revenue stalls in FY2027 and falls 3% in FY2028, and the fixed servicing and logistics base deleverages. Hurricane and wildfire losses run above the reinsurance budget, and cat-reinsurance costs climb. Rate cuts take roughly 100bp off the reinvestment yield on the ~$9bn bond book. Lender-placed attracts renewed regulatory scrutiny. The underlying pretax margin falls back to 8.3%, below FY2024's 8.4%, and rating agencies push capital retention up to 35% of incremental revenue.

base.margin_note: ebitda_margin = underlying pretax margin + 0.67 SBC + 1.85 D&A. Underlying pretax path 9.9% -> 10.3% by year 5, then flat: scale in Connected Living and claims automation offset by NII yield drift as rates fall and normal cat years.
base.narrative: The partnerships won in 2024-25 keep scaling, so Global Lifestyle grows at a low-double-digit rate in FY2026 and fades to the mid-single digits as they mature. Housing grows modestly on lender-placed and renters. Revenue +9% in FY2026 (H1 +10.3%), slowing to 3% by year 9. The underlying pretax margin sits at a cat-normalised 9.9% in FY2026, including the guided $71M adverse reserve development, and edges up to 10.3% as fixed costs are spread over more revenue. That gain is partly offset by portfolio yields drifting down. 30% of each revenue dollar added is held back as capital, which keeps tangible equity ex-AOCI at ~29% of revenue,, and the rest is paid out through buybacks and dividends.

bull.margin_note: Underlying pretax 10.3% (a benign H2 cat season on top of the H1 run-rate) rising to 11.5% by year 6.
bull.narrative: The trade-in and upgrade franchise and the combined mobile-plus-vehicle bundles keep winning carrier and OEM programmes in the US, Japan and Europe. AI-led claims and service automation lowers the cost to serve. Revenue grows at a high-single to low-double-digit rate for three years, and the underlying pretax margin climbs to 11.5% as Lifestyle mix rises and Housing takes rate on lender-placed. Capital intensity falls a little (25% of incremental revenue) because fee-based Lifestyle growth needs less statutory capital.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is raised from the 15% house default to 20% because Global Lifestyle rests on a small number of carrier and OEM contracts (a single-customer-style dependency) and Housing carries catastrophe tail risk. Base stays at 50%: it is H1-2026 actuals plus guidance. Bull is trimmed to 30% because it needs partner wins and margin expansion together, but the partnerships already signed make it credible.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
